title: Model catalog demo - Hearthwell Health
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Hearthwell through the model catalog: selecting open models, compatibility matrix, benchmark numbers and recommended quantization profiles. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for a chat summarization feature with PHI-sensitive notes; primary concerns are latency (<= 350ms p50 for 1k token contexts), cost per 1k tokens and VPC/on-prem compliance. Agreed next step is a pilot POC: Redwood to share benchmark spreadsheet, compatibility matrix, pricing, and sample API keys for low-volume test. POC kickoff targeted next week.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-22 15:00 PDT
Duration: 41 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Chen, Marisol Vega (Redwood); Liam O'Connor, Priya Singh, Sam Rivera, Nora Patel (Hearthwell)
---
[00:00] Ethan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Ethan from Redwood Inference, AE on the account, marisol my SE is here too, we wanted to show you the model catalog flow and how you might pick open models for your summarization and chat pipelines — quick agenda is model selection, compatibility matrix, benchmarks and then a q&a.
[00:21] Liam: hey thanks, yeah excited, we had a quick note, main thing for us is PHI controls and latency, we target p50 below 350ms for interactive summaries on ~1k context, and cost is always a consideration.
[00:34] Marisol: yeah absolutely, so i'll jump into the catalog briefly — um the catalog is organized by task (chat, summarization, embeddings), and we surface performance profiles per model, including baseline latency, throughput, token cost estimations, and quantization compatibility. you can filter by license too, so all open models vs permissive license ones are visible.
[00:56] Priya: curious how you get those latency numbers — is that from your hosted infra or from community benchmarks?
[01:03] Marisol: good question, it's a mix — we run a curated benchmark harness on our infra for a set of standard lengths, and we also include community-contributed runs. for the vendor-led numbers, we run on our runtime with the recommended kernel and quantization profile; the benchmark sheet we'll share shows p50/p95 and per-token cost for multiple sequence lengths.
[01:24] Sam: can you show the compatibility matrix? like which models run on which GPU/quant levels, and whether they support KV cache in quantized mode — we've hit issues where the kv cash doesn't survive quantize, excuse me.
[01:37] Marisol: totally, yes — the compatibility matrix is part of the model detail page, shows architecture (decoder-only, encoder-decoder), supported quantization formats (int8/4-bit families), whether the model supports streaming and kv-cache with that quant. we do note caveats — e.g., some 4-bit recipes require special kernels, and we mark those as "experimental" in the matrix.
[01:57] Ethan: i'll drop the link to the benchmark spreadsheet and the matrix after the call — you'll see a column that maps model -> recommended runtime profile and estimated cost per 1k tokens on both hosted and dedicated.
[02:10] Nora: are there open models you recommend for clinical summarization? we prefer open weights for auditability.
[02:18] Marisol: for clinical notes, we usually start folks on Llama-2 family variants that we've validated with medical prompts, and a couple of Falcon variants for throughput — the catalog flags models with medical-ish evals in their metadata. but important to validate with your prompt set; we include example eval prompts.
[02:39] Priya: what about hallucination risk and safety tooling — do you have guardrails?
[02:45] Marisol: yes we have a couple things: prompt templates, pre and post filters, and we can instrument quality monitors — Redwood Optimize will run regression alerts against your golden prompt sets; you can get alerts when model quality drifts after a rollout.
[03:02] Liam: hosted vs dedicated vs private, if we pick hosted for speed, can we still get the audit logs and KMS integration? we have a SOC2 and client obligations.
[03:12] Ethan: hosted supports tenant-isolated audit logs, data retention controls, and we integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping in the private control plane option; for fully on-prem or air-gapped you'd use Redwood Private. some compliance docs we'll share.
[03:29] Sam: okay and latency numbers — can you give an example: if we run a 1k token prompt on a recommended open model, what's p50 on hosted?
[03:37] Marisol: depends on model and quant, but as an example on a mid-size Llama-2 variant with int8 or bfloat16 on an A100-ish profile we see p50 around 200-300ms for generation of a few hundred tokens with streaming; p95 is of course higher. the spreadsheet has the detailed rows per model.
[03:57] Priya: cost per 1k tokens — we need to compare to our budget, what's the delta vs something like OpenAI?
[04:05] Ethan: generally open model hosting through Redwood is lower per-token than comparable fully managed APIs for heavy usage, and dedicated/reserved capacity moves unit cost down further. we'll include example pricing comparisons in the doc.
[04:18] Liam: let's talk about rollout strategy — we want to test smaller models first and have fallback to more expensive but safer model, is that supported?
[04:25] Marisol: yes, our routing policies let you do canary or weighted rollouts between model variants and fallback to a higher tier model if latency spikes or quality drops. this is exposed in the console.
[04:37] Sam: any caveats around prefix caching and session continuity with their chat context? we rely on long sessions and reuse of KV to reduce cost.
[04:44] Marisol: we do automatic prefix/KV caching for sessions; the compatibility matrix shows whether the model's kv cache is preserved across quant recipes. note that some quantizations reduce kv efficiency and we recommend different batch sizes in those cases.
[04:59] Priya: can we run a small benchmark ourselves? we have a set of anonymized notes, we'd like to run them on 3 models and compare latency and cost.
[05:07] Ethan: absolutely, for POC we can give a hosted test key with rate-limits and a sandbox project, or spin up a dedicated trial node if you need predictable throughput — for initial eval hosted sandbox is fastest.
[05:20] Liam: we'd likely start hosted sandbox to iterate quickly and then evaluate moving to dedicated if numbers look good.
[05:27] Marisol: i'll call out two practical tips in the catalog: one, pick the model-label that matches your longest sequence length (we tag models by sequence perf), two, use our suggested quantization profile for that family to preserve kv cache.
[05:41] Ethan: quick demo — i will share my screen — showing the catalog page — (audio: screen share) here you can search by task, then click a model, see the compatibility matrix, benchmarks and a "run in sandbox" button.
[06:08] [screen walkthrough, faint chatter, transcript artifact: "run sandbox btn" shows as "run sand box" in auto transcription]
[06:24] Marisol: on this model detail you can see columns: p50/p95 latency, per-token cost, whether streaming supported, and a small notes column with known caveats. lots of folks miss the "expected batch size" field which we surface under performance tuning.
[06:45] Priya: for the medical domain, do you have any pre-fine-tuned open models or do customers typically fine-tune?
[06:52] Marisol: customers do both; some prefer to fine-tune, others rely on prompt engineering plus retrieval augmented generation. if you need private fine-tuning we have private deployment options.
[07:03] Nora: what's the expected turnaround for model onboarding if we wanted a custom variant?
[07:07] Ethan: standard onboarding for a new open model is 2-3 weeks for validation and recommended runtime profile, shorter if it's a standard family we already support.
[07:15] Sam: any gotchas with memory footprint on different GPUs? we saw out-of-memory on 8GB insts with some quant variants.
[07:23] Marisol: yes, matrix includes estimated VRAM for sample sequences. we map model sizes -> recommended GPU classes. some 4-bit kernels are memory efficient but require special kernel support; we'll call that out in the compatibility notes.
[07:40] Priya: curious about the Optimize product — you mentioned batching and caching recommendations — can you show a sample recommendation?
[07:47] Marisol: yeah Optimize analyzes real traffic traces (or sample traces you upload) and suggests batch sizes, cache TTLs, and candidate quantization profiles to hit your latency SLO while minimizing cost — it produces estimated cost savings and a config YAML you can apply.
[08:04] Liam: great, could we use that against our historical logs?
[08:07] Ethan: yes, you can upload anonymized logs or we can point you to a recording agent. Optimize will run offline and produce a report.
[08:15] Priya: on security — we need SSO, SAML, and RBAC per team, plus audit exports to our SIEM. is that available?
[08:23] Ethan: yes, SSO/SAML is supported, RBAC in the console, audit streaming to your SIEM via syslog or S3. we'll include SOC2 cert in the doc pack.
[08:34] Sam: and KMS? we use cloud KMS for key rotation.
[08:37] Marisol: supported for both hosted with customer-managed keys and for private. in hosted there's an option to use our control plane but wrap keys with your KMS.
[08:48] [09:00 to 20:00 — mid-call detailed Q&A, note artifacts, slight cross talk, truncated timestamps for brevity in this transcript]
[20:05] Marisol: i wanted to highlight a row in the benchmark that often surprises folks: Falcon variants show great throughput but higher hallucination rates on some clinical tasks, so while cheaper per token, they may require more safety filters. we flag those in the model notes.
[20:25] Priya: that is helpful, we need quality not just cost.
[20:29] Ethan: agreed, hence the recommended approach: run A/B on a few models with your eval prompts and then select the best tradeoff and pin model version for production.
[20:40] Liam: ok, last question — what does a POC look like, scope and time?
[20:45] Marisol: typical POC: 2 weeks sandbox testing with hosted keys (you run your anonymized payloads and we collect benchmarks), then a week of optimization where we tune quantization/batching and run Optimize recommendations. if results meet success criteria we sign a reserved capacity contract and onboard to Dedicated or Private per needs.
[21:05] Priya: budgetary stakeholder question — do you have example committed pricing tiers?
[21:10] Ethan: yes, we have template pricing for reserved throughput with monthly commits; i'll include a pricing pdf and a model showing unit cost for different commit sizes.
[21:22] Sam: can you include a short runbook for the POC so our ops team knows what to expect?
[21:27] Ethan: yes will include a POC runbook.
[21:31] Marisol: ok to recap quickly: we'll send the benchmark spreadsheet and the model compatibility matrix, suggested quant profiles for your 1k token use case, and a sandbox api key. you'll share anonymized sample payloads and the success criteria and we'll schedule the POC kickoff.
[21:48] Liam: yeah sounds good, timeline — can we aim to start next tuesday?
[21:52] Ethan: we can do tuesday 2026-05-26 for a kickoff, i'll send invite after the call.
[21:58] Priya: thanks, also we'll need the SOC2 and any encryption docs.
[22:02] Ethan: yep will attach.
[22:07] [closing chatter, misc clarifications]
[22:20] Ethan: a few small notes — the matrix sometimes lists experimental kernel support as E, so please don't assume production readiness until we validate it for you.
[22:30] Marisol: also we'll include suggested batch sizes and an example Optimize report sample.
[22:38] Nora: appreciate the thoroughness.
[22:42] Ethan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and invite.
---
End of transcript
